qt: to the Commission Sakis Arnaoutoglou (S&D) Subject:

The 2026 Integrated Administration and Control System (IACS) procedure for submitting single applications for aid in Greece is plagued by serious delays and malfunctions, raising concerns among producers about the timely payment of common agricultural policy aid. The new myAGRO application only became operational on 4 August 2026 and the submission deadline was extended to 30 October 2026. Technical problems have been reported, as well as discrepancies between registries and difficulties in finalising applications, which means that legitimate beneficiaries may not receive their aid payments on time. Meanwhile, Regulation (EU) 2026/1768 provides Member States with more options, allowing early payment of advances of up to 75 %, to enhance rural liquidity. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.
Have the Greek authorities informed it about the number of finalised applications, the backlog and the ability and willingness to make advance payments under IACS 2026?
How does it intend to ensure that legitimate beneficiaries are not deprived of aid because of technical malfunctions or administrative delays that are not attributable to them?

What supervisory and technical assistance measures can it put into effect to ensure timely payments, reliable controls and full protection of European funds, in particular following the OPEKEPE revelations?
